AUTHORITY: docs/development/v3-governed-derived-purge-design.md sections 4.2 (all of it), 4.3 steps 6-9, 6 and 7 (gate 2, gate 3b option (b) contract, gate 4); docs/operations/v3-governed-derived-purge.md; sql/v3/migrations/016_v3_governed_derived_purge.sql (call its functions; never re-implement or bypass them; do NOT change 016). Build on the merged P2b1 code in scripts/operator/actions/v3-derived-generation-purge.sh, scripts/operator/lib/v3_generation_purge.py and v3_purge_transactions.py; extend, do not restructure.

PURGE P2 PLAN: P2a, P2b1 merged. P2b2a (THIS PR). P2b2b next: rewrite-<relation> with the systemd-run monitor and the rewrite branches of trap/restore-services. P2c: protected workflow. P2d: 1% rehearsal. Keep rewrite-<relation> refused with mode_not_implemented_until_p2b2b; design every shared piece (lease, trap, restore-services resolution, fence adoption) so P2b2b only adds the rewrite branch.

BUILD:
1. delete-<relation> for the four relations in the FK-safe order 016 enforces (system-search, economy-opportunity, body-mechanics, system-rating-vector). Requires the authenticated plan and the sealed verify-system-archetype-empty proof (path + SHA-256, as P2b1 defined). Holds the host lease /run/lock/edfinder-v3-derived-purge.lock (non-blocking flock) for its whole life. Opens or ADOPTS the relation's autovacuum fence via 016 (adopt an open AUTOVACUUM_DISABLED for the same relation; refuse with a different relation's fence open), re-reading XID/MultiXact ages against the ledgered ceilings before doing anything. Enables the gate 3b writer fence via 016 (purge_set_writer_fence + purge_recycle_writer_sessions + purge_verify_writer_fence, two-step commit-then-terminate-then-probe exactly as the gate 3b row says) unless an open verified fence for this purge already exists, and holds the pgBackRest schedule lock /run/lock/edfinder-v3-pgbackrest-schedule.lock (non-blocking flock) and refuses if any pgbackrest backup/verify process runs in the PostgreSQL container. Then runs a bounded loop of small 016 batches (v3_meta.purge_start_payload_batch / purge_derived_payload_batch; batch size <= 100000 and a lower per-relation bound from the plan) with a fixed wall-clock budget argument (bounded, default conservative). BEFORE EVERY BATCH: re-measure free bytes on the data filesystem and require >= 100 GB floor + 1.5 x the relation's per-batch peak growth reservation (take the reservation from the plan; if the plan has no rehearsal figure yet, use a conservative fixed reservation constant and record it); re-run the WAL-health gate (pg_wal on the data filesystem; no slot retaining WAL by wal_status extended/unreserved/lost or inactive; archiver failed_count unchanged since the dispatch's start snapshot AND last_failed_time not newer than last_archived_time); re-run the named-worker check; re-check autovacuum not running on the relation or its TOAST relation; re-check the controller (the GITHUB_RUN_ID / controller PID it was given is still alive -- design: a lost controller stops after at most one more batch with FAILED_STOP); wait, bounded, for no other backend holding backend_xid (reuse P2b1's wait_for_competing_writers) and record the wait. On any gate failure: start no further batch, append FAILED_STOP via 016 with the measured figures (integrity_failed only for published-survivor-count drift, pointer change or FK/index failure, per design section 6), exit. Committed batches stand; the next dispatch resumes from database counts. A batch-level monitor cancels the batch's own backend through v3_meta.cancel_purge_batch if the floor is crossed mid-batch. The matching delete-<relation> dispatch first resolves an open BATCH_STARTED from database evidence (committed or not by its recorded key range) before doing anything else. When the relation's target rows reach zero, report next mode rewrite-<relation> (refused until P2b2b) and leave the autovacuum fence OPEN (the rewrite verifies and restores it).
2. Exit/signal trap (design 4.2): record the exact running write-capable application container set (from deploy/v3-production/target-authority.json, not discovery) in both a SERVICES_QUIESCED-style ledger record where the design requires it and a root-owned host state file; under option (b) the API stays up and only the writer fence applies, so services are NOT stopped -- implement option (b) only, and keep the quiesce path refused with a clear code unless a future owner decision selects option (a). On EXIT/INT/TERM/HUP: signal the loop to stop after its current batch and wait for the loop process to exit; resolve any open BATCH_STARTED; then restore the writer fence to the ledgered prior value through 016 (commit, terminate the role's sessions, fresh-probe verify, append the verification) UNLESS a FAILED_STOP with integrity_failed=true exists (then restore nothing and leave the fence open); only after the restore is durable release the host lease. Never release the lease while the loop PID is alive.
3. restore-services: idempotent; first resolves any open BATCH_STARTED for this purge (cancel the recorded backend through cancel_purge_batch if PID+backend_start still live, wait until gone, then resolve from database evidence); leaves any open REWRITE_STARTED to P2b2b (refuse with rewrite_resolution_requires_p2b2b); then restores the writer fence from the ledgered prior value (set off, or unset/RESET, exactly as recorded) with the two-step verify. After a FAILED_STOP with integrity_failed=true it refuses unless given --acknowledge-failed-stop=<that event's sequence>, which it records in the payload.
4. abort-relation-<relation>: applies the free-space gate to the autovacuum it releases (floor + an autovacuum budget never below the relation's current heap+index bytes; report the shortfall), restores the ledgered prior autovacuum setting through 016's purge_set_relation_autovacuum, appends AUTOVACUUM_RESTORED with aborted:true and the measured headroom, leaves the relation logically emptied but not rewritten; status then reports the relation as waiting for rewrite.
5. Carried items (all required): (a) drop the python3 fallback in v3-derived-generation-purge.sh -- require python3.14 and emit the python314_required receipt otherwise; (b) bind deploy/v3-production/backup/pgbackrest-operation.sh into script_sha256 (or derive the expected wrapper hash from the git object at the claimed source SHA) so local drift fails closed; (c) compute wal_byte_delta for every successful non-status mode from the before/after LSNs with pg_wal_lsn_diff, and fail closed if it cannot be derived; (d) add the pgBackRest schedule-lock and process check to authorize/complete as well if the design requires it there.
6. Tests: extend tests/test_v3_derived_generation_purge_operator.py and the PG18 tests (tests/test_v3_governed_derived_purge.py or a new PG18 file using its fixtures) for: the loop starts no further batch after a floor or WAL-gate failure and appends FAILED_STOP, and a later dispatch resumes from counts; a lost controller stops after at most one more batch; the launcher does not return while the loop runs; the lease is never released while the loop PID is alive; the trap restores the writer fence only after the loop exits and never after an integrity FAILED_STOP; restore-services is idempotent, resolves an open batch first, and requires the acknowledgement after an integrity failure; a pooled session that reconnected during the fence is read-write after restore (prior value set off, and unset, as separate cases); fence adoption and the different-relation refusal; abort-relation's headroom gate; competing-writer bounded wait per batch; the four carried items; bash -n; no mutation on any preflight failure. PG18 tests may skip on the runner: report written-not-run. Keep the Finder PG18 CI lane under its 45-minute pytest bound: keep new PG18 tests small and fast.
7. Docs: extend docs/operations/v3-governed-derived-purge.md with the delete phase, trap, restore-services and abort procedures; CHANGES.md entry; update deploy/v3-production/f2d-operator-code.txt and its tests if new operator files are added.
